title: The Melancholic Gentleman and the Witty Traveler
summary: In the city of Basra lived an affluent merchant named Abu Ali, who fell into such a deep and persistent melancholy that he ceased to smile, closed his shop, and sat in his court...
keywords: tale of the melancholist and the sharper
full_text:
In the city of Basra lived an affluent merchant named Abu Ali, who fell into such a deep and persistent melancholy that he ceased to smile, closed his shop, and sat in his courtyard wrapped in black wool, weeping for no reason whatsoever. All the physicians of Basra prescribed bitter herb broths and bloodletting, but Abu Ali’s gloom only deepened.

A merry, traveling sharper from Cairo named Juha arrived in the city, heard of the merchant’s condition, and knocked upon his gate, claiming: 'I am a master physician who cures grief with a single word!'

Juha sat before the melancholic merchant, took out a polished brass whistle, and began to recount a series of the most preposterous, whimsical, and comical misadventures: of a donkey that sued his master for back wages, of a baker who baked a loaf of bread so large it had to be delivered on a four-wheeled cart with a team of oxen, and of a pompous magistrate who sat upon a basket of eggs!

Juha acted out every role with hilarious gestures, mimicking the voices with such razor-sharp timing and absurd dignity that Abu Ali’s lips twitched.

Suddenly, Abu Ali burst into a roaring, uncontrollable shout of laughter! He laughed until his turban slipped, tears of joy streamed down his cheeks, and his chest felt light as the morning breeze.

The black cloud of gloom evaporated from his spirit forever.

Abu Ali rewarded Juha with five hundred gold dinars, reopened his business, and declared that a spoonful of genuine laughter is worth ten thousand apothecary jars of bitter medicine.
moral: Laughter, good humor, and shared human sympathy are the truest medicines for melancholy.
